messages:
carmen (DevEx): Quick thread — noticed a reproducible duplicate-start when sampleapp performs a chunked upload and device rotates or network flaps.

carmen (DevEx): Steps: start chunked POST /v1/stream -> rotate screen or toggle wifi quickly -> server logs two start_token for same client session id. Seen on Pixel and OnePlus.

hao (Android): Is our retry interceptor re-executing the request on IOException? If so, streaming bodies are one-shot and will duplicate.

carmen (DevEx): Yes we have a RetryInterceptor that does a naive retry: catch(IOException) -> chain.call().client().newCall(req).execute().

neel (Platform): Short-term: mark chunked/streaming endpoints as non-retryable in SDK defaults (retryOnConnectionFailure=false for streaming client) and add a guard in RetryInterceptor to skip re-exec when request.body?.contentLength()==-1.

tara (QA): I'll add a small CI check in sampleapp: rotate mid-send and assert server saw exactly one start_token. Also will add a variant that simulates a 200-500ms network drop.

carmen (DevEx): Agreed. Longer term we should support an X-Idempotency-Key header so apps that want retries can opt-in and server can dedupe. I'll open PRs: interceptor guard + sampleapp tests + docs note.

ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1955 - "Chunked streaming + retry path duplicates start; classify streaming as non-retryable and add idempotency header"

hao (Android): thanks — will audit SDK interceptors for any newCall/execute patterns and replace with safe logic.

carmen (DevEx): great, landing the PR today.
